input.purpose: Urgent gas safety advice following report of a strong gas smell and a headache at 9 Birch Close
input.talking_points:
- Because the smell is strong and your wife has a headache, please get everyone (and any pets) out of the house now and stay out.
- Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away if you have not already. They are free, available 24/7 and will come out to make the supply safe.
- On your way out: leave doors and windows open. Do not use light switches, electrical appliances or the doorbell, and do not use naked flames or smoke. If you can reach the gas meter safely, turn the supply off at the meter (lever across the pipe).
- If your wife's headache, dizziness or nausea gets worse, or anyone feels unwell, get medical advice (NHS 111, or 999 if it is serious). Tell them about the possible gas/carbon monoxide exposure.
- Do not use the cooker, boiler or any gas appliance until an engineer says they are safe.
- Ask: have you already called 0800 111 999? Has anyone attended? Is anyone else in the property, and are there any pets?
- We are arranging a Gas Safe registered engineer to follow up after the emergency service has made it safe. We will text you the details.
- You will not be charged for this. Gas safety is the landlord's legal responsibility.
